chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted and Glorified, did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and are steadfast.
He has authority only over those who take him as an ally and those who associate partners with him.

key_terms.تَعَمَّدُوا: Were steadfast, persevered, or committed deliberately

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this narration within the Imami doctrine of *al-Isbat wa al-Takfir* (affirmation and denial), emphasizing that Satan's *sultan* (authority) is contingent upon human free will and spiritual vigilance rather than absolute dominion. This distinction reinforces the Shia theological stance that true believers (*mu'minun*) are shielded from his sway through adherence to the Imams, while those who ally with him (*mu'alliqun bihi*) fall under his influence, a concept deeply rooted in the exegetical tradition of the Ahl al-Bayt.
